description: If someone is entrusted with a closed container containing property but without the authority to open it, and they dishonestly or with mischief in mind break it open or unfasten it, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to three years, a fine, or both.

description: If someone uses a false mark in a way prohibited by the previous section and cannot prove that they had no intent to defraud, they will be punished as if they committed an offense under that section.

offenceName: Removing destroying or defacing property mark with intent to cause injury
description: If someone intentionally removes, destroys, defaces, or alters any property mark, knowing it might cause harm to someone, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to one year, a fine, or both.

offenceName: Counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes
description: If someone counterfeits or is involved in the process of counterfeiting currency notes or banknotes, they can be punished with life imprisonment or imprisonment for up to ten years, along with a fine.

offenceName: Using as genuine forged or counterfeit currency-notes or bank-notes
description: If someone knowingly sells, buys, receives, or uses as genuine any forged or counterfeit currency notes or banknotes, they can be punished with life imprisonment or imprisonment for up to ten years, along with a fine.

offenceName: Possession of forged or counterfeit currency-notes or bank-notes
description: If someone knowingly possesses forged or counterfeit currency notes or banknotes with the intent to use them as genuine or allow others to use them as genuine, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to seven years, a fine, or both.

offenceName: Making or possessing machinery, instrument or material for forging or counterfeiting currency-notes or bank-notes
description: If someone makes, uses, buys, sells, or possesses any machinery or material for the purpose of forging or counterfeiting currency or banknotes, they can be punished with life imprisonment or imprisonment for up to ten years, along with a fine.

description: If a man deceives an unmarried woman into believing that she is lawfully married to him and engages in a relationship or sexual intercourse with her based on that false belief, he can be punished with imprisonment for up to ten years and may also be fined.

offenceName: Marrying again during the life-time of a husband or wife
description: If someone marries again while their previous husband or wife is still alive, and such a marriage is considered void, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to seven years and may also be fined. Cited by Musstt Rehana Begum vs The State Of Assam Surajma

description: If someone commits the offense of marrying again without disclosing their previous marriage to the new spouse, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to ten years and may also be fined.

offenceName: A person with fraudulent intention going through the ceremony of being married knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married
description: If someone dishonestly or fraudulently undergoes a marriage ceremony, knowing they are not lawfully married, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to seven years and may also be fined.

offenceName: Adultery

offenceName: Enticing or taking away or detaining with a criminal intent a married woman
description: If someone takes or lures away a woman who they know is married to another man, with the intention that she engages in illicit relations with anyone else, or if they hide or detain her with that intention, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to two y

offenceName: Defamation against the President or the Vice-president or the Governor of a State or Administrator of a Union Territory or a Minister in respect of his conduct in the discharge of his public functions when instituted upon a complaint made by the Public Prosecutor
description: If someone defames another person, they can be punished with up to two years of simple imprisonment, a fine, or both.

description: If someone prints or engraves any content, knowing or having good reason to believe that it is defamatory about a person, they can be punished with up to two years of simple imprisonment, a fine, or both.

offenceName: Sale of printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter, knowing it to contain such matter against the President or the Vice-President or the Governor of a State or Administrator of a Union territory or a Minister in respect of his conduct in the discharge of his public functions when instituted upon a complaint made by the Public Prosecutor
description: If someone knowingly sells or offers for sale any printed or engraved material containing defamatory content, they can be punished with up to two years of simple imprisonment, a fine, or both. Cited by Gambhirsinh R Dekare vs Falgunbhai Chimanbhai Patel and An

offenceName: Insult intended to provoke breach of the peace
description: If someone intentionally insults another person, knowing it could provoke them to disturb public peace or commit another offense, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to two years, a fine, or both. Cited by Nazma vs Javed at Anjum Dinesh Tiwari vs Sta

offenceName: False statement, rumour, etc., circulated with intent to cause mutiny or offence against the public peace

offenceName: Criminal intimidation by Anonymous communication or having taken precaution to conceal whence the threat comes
description: If someone engages in criminal intimidation using an anonymous communication or hides their identity to issue threats, they can be punished with imprisonment for up to two years, along with the punishment prescribed for the offense of criminal intimidation.

offenceName: Act caused by inducing a person to believe that he will be rendered an object of Divine displeasure
description: If someone tries to make another person do something they are not legally obligated to do or refrain from something they are legally entitled to do by falsely claiming that divine displeasure will befall them or someone they care about, they can be punished wi

offenceName: Uttering any word or making any gesture intended to insult the modesty of a woman, etc.
description: If someone intentionally tries to insult a woman's modesty by using offensive words, gestures, or actions, or intrudes on her privacy, they can be punished with up to three years of simple imprisonment, along with a fine.

offenceName: Appearing in a public Place, etc., in a State of intoxication, and causing annoyance to any person
description: If someone, while intoxicated, behaves in a way that annoys others in a public or restricted area, they can be punished with up to 24 hours of simple imprisonment, or a fine up to ten rupees, or both.

offenceName: Tampering documents stored within a computer system
description: This section deals with intentional alteration, deletion, or manipulation of computer source documents. It targets unauthorized interference with system files or code. Such actions compromise system integrity and reliability.

offenceName: Offences associated with computers or any act outlined in Section 43
description: Covers acts like hacking, data theft, introducing viruses, or damaging systems. It builds on Section 43 but adds criminal liability when intent or dishonesty is involved. Widely used in cybercrime cases.

offenceName: Dishonestly receiving a stolen computer source or device
description: Targets individuals who knowingly receive stolen digital devices or data. Similar to receiving stolen property under IPC but applied to digital assets. Focus is on dishonest intent.

offenceName: Identity theft
description: Involves misuse of someone’s digital identity such as passwords, digital signatures, or biometric data. Common in phishing and online fraud. Protects personal digital credentials.

offenceName: Cheating by personation
description: Applies when someone impersonates another person online to commit fraud. Includes fake profiles, scam emails, or impersonation in financial transactions. Frequently seen in online scams.

offenceName: Invading privacy
description: Deals with capturing, publishing, or transmitting private images without consent. Focus is on violation of bodily privacy using digital means. Relevant in cases of voyeurism and misuse of images.

offenceName: Cyber terrorism
description: Covers acts threatening national security using computer resources. Includes attacks on critical infrastructure or attempts to destabilize the nation. Considered one of the most serious cyber offences.

offenceName: Sending explicit or obscene material in electronic form
description: Targets publishing or transmitting obscene content online. Applies to websites, social media, and messaging platforms. Focus is on public morality and digital content regulation.

offenceName: Sending material containing sexually explicit acts through electronic means
description: Stronger provision than Section 67, specifically for sexually explicit content. Addresses distribution of explicit videos or acts. Penalty is more severe due to gravity of content.

offenceName: Depicting children in sexually explicit form and sharing such material
description: Deals with child pornography and exploitation. Includes browsing, downloading, or distributing such content. Highly stringent due to protection of minors.

offenceName: Failure to preserve and retain the information by intermediaries
description: Applies to intermediaries like ISPs or platforms failing to retain data as required. Important for investigation and evidence collection. Ensures accountability of digital service providers.

offenceName: Failure to comply orders of the Controller
description: Covers non-compliance with directions issued by the Controller of Certifying Authorities. Ensures regulatory oversight of digital certification processes. Applies to authorized entities.

offenceName: Failure to intercept, monitor or decrypt data as per government instructions
description: Applies when entities refuse lawful government orders for surveillance or decryption. Important for national security and law enforcement. Non-compliance leads to strict punishment.

offenceName: Failure to block public access of information as per government instructions
description: Deals with non-compliance in blocking websites or content as ordered by government. Commonly used for banning harmful or illegal content. Ensures enforcement of digital restrictions.

offenceName: Failure to monitor and collect traffic data for cyber security
description: Focuses on failure to assist government in monitoring traffic data for cybersecurity. Helps in threat detection and prevention. Heavy financial penalty reflects importance.

offenceName: Secures access or attempts to secure access to a protected system
description: Applies to unauthorized access to critical systems declared as protected. Includes government or strategic infrastructure systems. Considered a serious breach.

offenceName: Misrepresentation to the Controller or Certifying Authority
description: Covers providing false information to obtain digital certificates or approvals. Undermines trust in digital authentication systems. Focus is on integrity of certification.

offenceName: Breach of confidentiality and privacy
description: Targets unauthorized disclosure of information accessed during official duties. Applies to professionals handling sensitive data. Protects confidentiality obligations.

offenceName: Disclosure of information in breach of lawful contract
description: Deals with sharing personal information in violation of contractual agreements. Common in corporate or service provider contexts. Ensures data protection compliance.

offenceName: Falsely publishing electronic signature certificate
description: Applies when fake or unauthorized digital signature certificates are issued or published. Impacts trust in digital transactions. Focus is on authenticity.

offenceName: Publication for fraudulent purposes
description: Covers use of digital certificates or publications with intent to defraud. Includes misuse of credentials for illegal gain. Ensures accountability in digital communications.

offenceName: Penetrative sexual assault
description: As per section 3 of the POCSO Act, 2012: penetrative sexual assault on a child. Punishment is prescribed under section 4 (not less than ten years, may extend to imprisonment for life, and fine; with enhanced minimum for child below sixteen years).

offenceName: Punishment for penetrative sexual assault
description: Section 4: whoever commits penetrative sexual assault shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine; with further minimum twenty years for assault on child below sixteen years of age.

offenceName: Aggravated penetrative sexual assault
description: Section 5 defines aggravated penetrative sexual assault (including specified categories such as police officer, armed forces, public servant, institutional contexts, gang assault, use of weapons, grievous hurt, child below twelve, relative/domestic contexts, etc.).

offenceName: Punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault
description: Section 6: rigorous imprisonment not less than twenty years, may extend to imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life), and fine, or with death.

offenceName: Sexual assault
description: Section 7: sexual assault on a child (physical contact with sexual intent without penetration as defined in the Act).

offenceName: Punishment for sexual assault
description: Section 8: imprisonment not less than three years but which may extend to five years, and fine.

offenceName: Aggravated sexual assault
description: Section 9 defines aggravated sexual assault (including police, forces, public servant, institutional settings, gang assault, weapons, grievous hurt, disability, repeat, child below twelve, relative/domestic, etc.).

offenceName: Punishment for aggravated sexual assault
description: Section 10: imprisonment not less than five years but which may extend to seven years, and fine.

offenceName: Sexual harassment
description: Section 11: sexual harassment of a child (words, sounds, gestures, exhibition, stalking/contact, threats involving depiction of child, enticement for pornography, etc., with sexual intent).

offenceName: Punishment for sexual harassment
description: Section 12: imprisonment which may extend to three years and fine.

offenceName: Use of child for pornographic purposes
description: Section 13: use of a child in any form of media for sexual gratification including representation of sexual organs, simulated sexual acts, indecent or obscene representation.

offenceName: Punishment for using child for pornographic purposes
description: Section 14: imprisonment not less than five years and fine; on second or subsequent conviction not less than seven years and fine; additional punishment for linked penetrative/aggravated/sexual offences as prescribed.

offenceName: Punishment for storage of pornographic material involving child
description: Section 15: storage/possession of child pornography — fines for failure to delete/report; imprisonment up to three years or fine or both for possession for transmission; higher minima for commercial storage (up to seven years on subsequent conviction).

offenceName: Abetment of an offence
description: Section 16 defines abetment of an offence under the Act (instigation, conspiracy, intentional aid including trafficking-related facilitation).

offenceName: Punishment for abetment
description: Section 17: whoever abets an offence under the Act, if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment, shall be punished with punishment provided for that offence.

offenceName: Punishment for attempt to commit an offence
description: Section 18: attempt punishable with imprisonment up to one-half of imprisonment for life or one-half of the longest term provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both.

offenceName: Punishment for failure to report or record a case
description: Section 21: failure to report under section 19 or record under section 19(2) — imprisonment up to six months or fine or both; in-charge failing to report subordinate offence — up to one year and fine.

offenceName: Punishment for false complaint or false information
description: Section 22: false complaint or false information against any person in respect of offences under sections 3, 5, 7 or 9 with prescribed intent — imprisonment up to six months or fine or both; separate clause for false complaint by adult against a child.

offenceName: Punishment for contravention of media reporting restrictions
description: Section 23(4): contravention of sub-sections (1) or (2) regarding media reporting on child — imprisonment not less than six months but which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
